faq.q: What happens at the Lantern Festival?
faq.a: It falls on the 15th day of the Lunar New Year, under the first full moon. Families in China and beyond hang and carry lanterns, eat sweet rice balls called tangyuan and guess lantern riddles.
asks: When is the Chinese Lantern Festival?

faq.a: A Thai festival on the full moon, usually in November. People float krathongs, little boats of banana leaves with candles and flowers, to thank the water and let go of worries.
asks: Why do Thai people float candles?

faq.q: Why do people light lamps at festivals?
faq.a: In many cultures light stands for hope, goodness and knowledge winning over darkness. Lights also make long dark nights feel warm and joyful.
asks: Why is light important in festivals?

faq.a: On 13 December in Sweden and other Nordic countries, children sing songs in candlelit processions, and one girl wears a crown of candles, during the darkest time of year.
Kwanzaa is an African American celebration of family and culture from 26 December to 1 January. Each night a candle is lit on a kinara for one of seven values, such as unity.

facts: The Lantern Festival is held on the 15th day of the first month of the Chinese lunar calendar.
Hanukkah lasts eight nights, with one more candle lit each night.
Kwanzaa runs from 26 December to 1 January and celebrates seven principles.

quiz.why: At Loy Krathong in Thailand, people float krathongs with candles on rivers and lakes.
